subject: ogre-faced spider
title: This Spider Has No Ears. It Catches Flying Insects by Sound

scenes.text: This spider has no ears. It hunts by sound.
The ogre-faced spider hangs upside down at night, a silk net stretched between its front legs.
When an insect flies past behind it, it flips backward and nets it in mid-air.
Scientists covered its eyes. It caught flying prey just as well.
It listens with its legs. Tiny slits there pick up wingbeats from over six feet away.
Those huge eyes, the biggest of any spider, are only for prey on the ground.

description:
The ogre-faced spider, Deinopis spinosa, has no ears, yet it snatches flying insects out of the air behind its back by sound alone.
In a 2020 study in Current Biology, spiders flipped backward and cast their nets at low tones in the range of insect wingbeats, played from a speaker about two meters away. They hear with slit-shaped sensors in their legs. With their eyes covered they could no longer catch prey walking below them, but caught flying prey just as well. The spider's two big eyes are the largest of any known spider.
Which is stranger: hearing with your legs, or hunting with a net? Comment below.
first_comment: It also reacts to much higher tones it never strikes at. The researchers' guess: it is listening for the birds that eat it. What would you do with ears in your legs?
